query: How should safety-incident items be worded and what recall window (e.g., 7, 30, 90 days) yields valid, comparable reporting across sectors and age bands?

response.query: How should safety-incident items be worded and what recall window (e.g., 7, 30, 90 days) yields valid, comparable reporting across sectors and age bands?
response.answer: Safety-incident items should be clear, concise, and specific. A 30-day recall window is commonly used for valid, comparable reporting across sectors and age bands.

results.title: Operation and Certification of Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems
results.content: Docket Title | Document ID | Comments || Operation and Certification of Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems | [FAA-2015-0150-4721](https://www.regulations.gov/document/FAA-2015-0150-4721) | [24](https://www.regulations.gov/document/FAA-2015-0150-4721/comment) |  |. On February 23, 2015, as part of its ongoing efforts to integrate UAS operations in the NAS and in accordance with section 333 of [Public Law 112-95](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/112/public/95), the FAA issued the NPRM proposing to amend its regulations to adopt specific rules for the operation of small UAS in the NAS. Due to the lack of an onboard pilot, small UAS operations cannot be conducted in accordance with many of the FAA's current operating regulations, codified in [14 CFR part 91](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/part-91), that apply to general aviation. The FAA notes that the small unmanned aircraft flight will also have to comply with all other applicable requirements of this rule, including the prohibition on flight over people who are not directly participating in the small UAS operation (discussed in section III.E.3.b.iv of this preamble).
